issue_context.title: Add device trigger support to the media_player integration
issue_context.body:
Add [device trigger](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/en/device_automation_trigger.html) support to the media_player integration.

Device triggers are part of [Device Automations](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/en/device_automation_index.html), a new concept that was [recently launched](https://www.home-assistant.io/blog/2019/09/18/release-99/#device-automations) to make automations more user friendly.

Device automations consist of three different parts: triggers, triggers and triggers. This issue is about the trigger part.

To get started with this issue, you will need to set up a Home Assistant development environment. The easiest approach is to get started using [a dev container](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/en/development_environment.html#developing-with-devcontainer).

Once you have a development environment set up, run the following and follow the instructions:

```python
python3 -m script.scaffold device_trigger
```

_(This issue is part of #27008)_

Because media player is so shitty designed, this is not correct. What if we go from STATE_PLAYING ot STATE_OFF ? 

Heck, what does STATE_ON even mean? is it a catch all for playing/paused/idle ?

Thinking about it now I am pretty sure a media_player can turn off from any state (playing/paused/idle/on).
Therefore all of these states are possible from_states or what do you think?
No, I do not think that STATE_ON is a catch for all, it just means that the media_player is active.
Or am I missing something?
Right. But if a media player is playing and then turned off, we go from state `playing` to `off`. That will not be caught by this device trigger.

Should I change just this device trigger or all of them? By changing them I mean to spare the `from_state` e.g. like this:
https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant/blob/36796ef64974eea1fe365a7d38601aa745fd841f/homeassistant/components/cover/device_trigger.py#L174-L182
turn on and off are features that need to be enabled before they are supported.
